LAWS OF RHODE ISLAND.
State Of Rhode Island and Providence
Plantations.


In General Assembly Oct. Sess. A. D. 1826.
AN ACT in amendment Of an act entitled An Act providing for the
relief, support, employment and removal of the Poor.

SECTION 1. BE it enacted by the General Assembly, and by The authority thereof, That if any person shall reside in any town in the State, not being legally settled in that or any other town in the State, and shall become, or be likely to become chargeable to that town where such person shall reside, or who shall in the opinion of the town council of such town, be person of bad fame and reputation, and an unsuitable person to become an inhabitant thereof it shall and may be lawful for the town council of such town, upon complaint of any one or more of the overseers of the Poor of such town, to order such person to depart from and out of such town within such time as the said town council, in their discretion, may appoint; and if the person so ordered shall not depart from such town within the time appointed as aforesaid, or having so departed shall voluntarily return thither without leave first obtained from the town council for so doing, such person shall be fined by the town council not exceeding seven dollars, to and for the use of the poor of such town; and in default of paying the same at the time appointed by the said town council, shall be committed to the work house, bridewell, or asylum, (if any there be in the town,) to be there kept in close confinement or to labour; or the town council may bind out such person to service to any citizen of the United States, for any term not exceeding one year; or such person may be publicly whipped, not exceeding twenty nine stripes, at the discretion of the town council. And shall be subject to the like penalty and punishment on every repetition of such offence.

Sec: 2. And be it further enacted, That the nineteenth section of the act to which this is in amendment, be and the same is hereby repealed.


True copy Witness,

HENRY BOWEN, sec'ry.

MONDAY MORNING, NOVEMBER 6, 1826.

It is expected, says the Philadelphia papers, Mr. Sergeant, his private Secretary Mr. [Name] and the Secretary of the Mission Mr. Hester, will sail, in the sloop of war Hornet, Vera Cruz tomorrow.

New Jersey Patriot, states that the Dissertations of the Hon. C. F. Mercer, pronounced in essence of the Cliosophic and American Societies in September last, is now in the [Number] and viii appear in the course of the next month.

It is stated in the New-York Commercial Advertiser, that there are now forty cases of small pox on Staten Island, but there have been about one third of that number of deaths from this loathsome disease, in short time past.

A destructive FIRE took place at Utica, N. Y. Monday last. Seven of the most valuable stores in the village were laid in ashes; most of such, however, were insured. The amount of damage has not been ascertained, but supposed to be about $4,000.

The subject of the expediency of erecting a barrage in the city of Philadelphia, was to be considered at public meeting of the citizens on Wednesday last, but adjourned without deciding upon any plan.

A Senator in Congress is to be chosen for Pennsylvania at the next meeting of the Legislature. Samuel D. Ingham, esq. is spoken of with confidence to fill the place, to secure which, the Democratic Press says a number of voters are to attend at Harrisburg in December. The Press must be wrong.—The Legislature of Pennsylvania can stand in need of no boring when Ingham is candidate. As well might it be said that the people required boring when Mercer claimed their suffrages.

A snow storm commenced at New York early in the morning of Thursday last, and continued without intermission through the day.

CHESAPEAKE AND OHIO CANAL.

Agreeably to public notice, a number of citizens assembled on Friday, the 10th November at the Exchange, when Jacob Small, Esq. Mayor of the city, was called to the chair, and B. G. Howard, appointed Secretary. The following resolution was offered by Mr. Thomas Ellicott, and adopted:

That the interest of the city of Baltimore requires that she should be represented in the Convention to be held at Washington on the 9th day of December next, on the subject of the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal, and that the Chairman be authorized to appoint eight delegates to attend said Convention.

The meeting then adjourned.

JACOB SMALL, Chairman.
B. G. Howard, Sec'y, Balt. timer.
